findings: Buys: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it bought beat SPY by 1.09% on average (61 buys, 61% of them ahead of SPY; t = 2.6, significant at 5%).
Sells: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it sold beat SPY by 0.52%, so selling gave that up (130 sells; t = -1.4, within noise).
Decision IC: on the 33 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of -0.013 with the next five days' returns (IC IR -0.09, t = -0.5, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 49 decision days had a mean rank IC of 0.068 with the next five days' returns (t = 2.1, significant at 5%).
Factor exposures: market 0.33 (t 17.3), size -0.12 (t -4.5), growth -0.28 (t -6.8), momentum 0.03 (t 1.9); together they explain 71% of the daily variation (R²).
Of its +2.9% a year over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market -6.4%, growth +4.9%, size +0.3%, momentum +0.2%; the alpha left is +3.9% a year (t = 0.9, within noise).
Verdict: the exposures account for -1.0% a year of it, and the +3.9% a year left over is not significant: one period of daily returns cannot tell it from luck.
P&L: +$4,112 in all, +$3,170 from 49 positions and +$942 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$4,845, 11 positions); 3-5 days lost the most (-$4,047, 8 positions).
By sector: Health Care made the most (+$4,750, 14 positions); Technology lost the most (-$1,459, 2 positions).
By stock: LLY made the most (+$1,925, 3 positions); HON lost the most (-$1,116, 3 positions).
By market regime of the previous close: risk-on 11 days -0.2% (SPY -5.1%); neutral 6 days -0.8% (SPY -3.3%); uncertain 162 days -1.7% (SPY -19.0%); risk-off 72 days +7.0% (SPY +9.5%).
News: 10 positions opened on news made +$2,865, the other 39 +$305; 7 positions closed on news made -$64; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys beat SPY by 2.72% (t 3.7).

Concentration: the gains are spread out (the best two positions made 23% of them) but winners and losers nearly cancel, so the best two made 97% of the net P&L; the best was XOM bought 2022-01-04 and sold 2022-01-26, +$1,616. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned +2.5% instead of +4.1%.
